text: `click.prompt` catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and `EOFError` from the input function and re-raises `click.Abort` (a `RuntimeError` subclass, defined in `src/click/exceptions.py`). See `src/click/termui.py` lines 135-150: `except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError): ... raise Abort()`. The docstring states the same ("If the user aborts the input by sending a interrupt signal, this function will catch it and raise a :exc:`Abort` exception.").
`fs_enc` is set to the string `"ascii"` (see `src/click/_unicodefun.py` lines 8-13: `except Exception: fs_enc = "ascii"`).

#1 (required flag not enforced, src/click/core.py): root cause identified — Option.__init__ gives every flag a default of False, so a required flag's value is never "missing". Fix in progress, ETA ~8 min.

#4 (echo with no stdout/stderr streams): root cause identified — _default_text_stdout()/stderr() return None when sys.stdout/sys.stderr are None (e.g. pythonw), and echo/ProgressBar/pager then crash with AttributeError. Fix in progress across _compat.py, _termui_impl.py, utils.py, ETA ~12 min.
`echo` is imported from `click.utils` (`from .utils import echo` in src/click/__init__.py).
`TypeError("Cannot have two nargs < 0")` — raised in `_unpack_args` when a second `nargs < 0` position is encountered (src/click/parser.py line 94).
